page: Amazon Web Services r6i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz, it supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 512 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor architecture includes support for AVX-512 vector instruction extensions, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic primitives including AES-NI and SHA extensions. Networking throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute capabilities alongside memory capacity. The instance achieves strong tier placements in multi-core stress-ng evaluation (61,949.73), overall PassMark CPU score (57,729.17), and clang software compilation (40,752.0). Database performance is pronounced, evidenced by a strong result in PassMark database operations at 26,616.49. Static web serving throughput reaches 45.76 GB/sec. Single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1,688.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,893.89), place in the middle 50% category, showing that parallel multi-core scaling rather than single-thread clock speed drives overall system throughput.

Hardware resource tradeoffs include the complete absence of local bundled instance storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached Amazon EBS or remote storage services for persistent data volumes. In addition, no hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this server. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of memory and dedicated core count on a single node, which minimizes coordination overhead for large single-system memory applications compared to scaling across multiple smaller nodes.

The r6i.16xlarge configuration is suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Recommended target use cases include in-memory databases such as Redis, large relational database instances, distributed big-data processing platforms, large-scale software build systems, and enterprise data analytics pipelines requiring significant memory footprints alongside sustained multi-threaded execution.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by Intel Xeon 8375C processors operating at 3.5 GHz on the Nitro System. The server provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Baseline network bandwidth is 25 Gbps. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU hardware, requiring external network-attached volumes for data persistence. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-quartile performance in multi-core compute tests, clang software compilation, PassMark database operations, and static web serving throughput, while single-core processing aligns with median performance tiers. The configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-dense deployments by centralizing large-memory operations on a single host. Primary workload fits include enterprise relational databases, in-memory caching systems, big data processing frameworks, and distributed analytics pipelines.
